title: A short composer moves its tools into existing rows instead of dropping them
context: On a short panel (844x390 with a 200pt keyboard gives the sheet 186pt) the composer dropped the format bar, and with it the only Undo on Android, and the photo rail dropped its Add photo tile. The editor measured 86pt there against a 76.8pt three-line floor an existing test enforces, so there is no room for another 36pt row.
options: reduce the minimum writing lines so the bar and rail fit as extra rows
move the format bar into the header row in place of the title when short, put a slim Add photo tile in the bar's trailing slot when the rail has no room, and let the toggles scroll horizontally
leave the tools hidden and rely on typed Markdown
outcome: Move the tools into existing rows. Not roomy: header row becomes close, format bar, Save, with the title omitted; the header grows 31 to 36pt and the editor keeps three lines. The rail sits below the surface only when its budget reaches 72pt, otherwise it renders a 36x36 slim Add tile inside the bar. The rail is wrapped in a GlobalKey so a pick started from the slim tile survives the relayout when the system picker closes the keyboard. Ruling W3 of the fix-wave spec.
